verdict.justification: Both deliverables compile 33 wells across all eight requested systems, include the required data and screening columns, and identify the same seven qualifying wells. A is more decision-ready because its potential-wells tab explicitly ranks the candidates, labels the top three options, and provides well-specific PM comments rather than leaving prioritization solely in the email. A also identifies discrepancies between the factsheet narratives and well tables, specifically flagging Farmer City Well 7 for confirmation before relying on it. Its treatment of pumpage is more careful: “please do not quote them as capacity,” whereas B describes Well 9 as having “proven production” and calls the Farmer City leaders “the only qualifying wells with substantial reported pumpage” without defining that distinction. A provides stronger source traceability within the workbook through water-system identifiers and detailed screening and data-limitations notes. Although A's email is longer than necessary and includes optional hydrogen-demand context, its clearer prioritization and more explicit diligence requirements make it the stronger professional handoff.
